The first step compares y with x₃; the second expands y. For f=x² and inputs 0,3,6, the average input is two and the inequality is 4≤9, checking the weight arithmetic.

Induction to any finite number

For k=1 equality holds; k=2 is the definition. Assume the claim for k−1 terms. For k terms write t=θₖ. If t=1, all other weights vanish and equality holds. If t<1, set y=Σᵢ<k θᵢxᵢ/(1−t). Its normalized weights sum to one, so y∈D.

The last step applies induction to y and multiplies back by 1−t, restoring the weights. Zero weights cause no difficulty; the possible zero denominator was separated first. The expectation version is an integral extension requiring existence assumptions, not an automatic consequence for arbitrary infinite mixtures.

The plotted variance is an algebraic identity: for , the gap equals . It is a weighted average of squared deviations and requires no probability background.

4.2 一阶判据：切线是全局下界4.2 First-order criterion: tangent lower bounds

用定义直接展开平方很容易，但复杂函数未必方便。若函数可微，可以改问：在某点的线性近似是否压在整个图像下方？对开放凸域 D 上的可微函数，凸性等价于

为什么两种条件等价？

先假设凸。令 z=x+θ(y−x)，由定义 f(z)≤(1−θ)f(x)+θf(y)。移项、除以 θ>0，再令 θ↓0，可微性把左边变成方向导数：

反向设全局下界成立，取 为基点，明确写两次：

第一式乘 ，第二式乘 后相加。梯度前的向量为 ，留下 ，即凸性。

因此在无约束的开放域中，若有 ∇f(x)=0，则 x 全局最优。非凸函数的驻点没有这个保证。带约束时梯度不必为零：例如在 [1,∞) 上最小化 x²，最优点 1 的导数为 2。

不可微时仍可构造全局下界

若 f 不可微，仍可能有向量 g 满足 f(y)≥f(x)+gᵀ(y−x) 对所有 y 成立，称 g 为 x 处的。例如 |x| 在零点的所有 g∈[−1,1] 都给出这样的下界。求零点处全部次梯度，只需解 对所有实数 。 时要求 ， 时要求 ，两者合并为 ；反向代入可直接验证充分性。每个斜率给一条经过原点、压在整个绝对值图像下方的支撑直线。

先构造正面下界：对 在 的切线为 ，差为 。请独立在 处构造一次，再做下面的驻点反例。

练习

提示

解答与核对

零点切线为零，但 y<0 时 y³<0，函数位于切线下方，违背凸函数的一阶判据。x³ 在整个 R 上也不凸。

The definition works easily for squares but can be awkward for other functions. For a differentiable function, ask whether its local linear approximation lies below the whole graph. On an open convex D, convexity is equivalent to

The is fixed at x, yet gives a bound for every y. For f=x² at x=1, the line is 2y−1 and the gap is (y−1)²≥0. Differentiability alone gives a local approximation; convexity makes it a global bound.

Why are the conditions equivalent?

Assume convexity. Let z=x+θ(y−x); then f(z)≤(1−θ)f(x)+θf(y). Rearrange, divide by θ>0 and let θ decrease to zero. Differentiability identifies the directional derivative:

Conversely assume the lower-bound inequality. Apply it at z=(1−θ)x+θy with endpoints x,y. Weight the inequalities by 1−θ and θ and add. The gradient terms cancel since (1−θ)(x−z)+θ(y−z)=0, leaving exactly the convexity inequality.

Thus a zero gradient of a at an interior unconstrained point guarantees a global minimum. Nonconvex stationary points lack that guarantee. With constraints the gradient need not vanish: x² on [1,∞) is minimized at one with derivative two.

Global lower bounds without differentiability

At a nondifferentiable point, a vector g satisfying f(y)≥f(x)+gᵀ(y−x) for every y is a . For |x| at zero every g∈[−1,1] works. A subgradient is defined by a global inequality, not by arbitrarily filling in a missing derivative.

For the converse criterion, write both lower bounds at the same base :

Weight by and add. The gradient coefficient is , leaving convexity.

For the subgradients of at zero, solve for every real . Positive requires and negative requires . Conversely every works.

Before the counterexample, construct a successful bound: at base two has gap . Independently construct the bound at base minus one; it is .

The first-order condition compares all point pairs. For continuously twice differentiable functions on an open convex D, a local curvature test suffices: convexity is equivalent to an everywhere PSD Hessian.

On a segment let φ(t)=f(x+t(y−x)). Its second derivative is (y−x)ᵀH(y−x). PSD H makes φ″≥0, so the one-variable slope is nondecreasing and the convexity inequality holds on every segment. Conversely, convexity bounds midpoint values by endpoint averages; divide their symmetric difference by squared step length and take limits to obtain nonnegative curvature in every direction.

Since z is interior, both endpoints remain in the domain for small h. Midpoint convexity makes the difference quotient nonnegative; Chapter 2 second-order expansion identifies its limit.

Three one-variable functions, differentiated explicitly

For f(x)=eᵃˣ with fixed real a, each differentiation multiplies by a. The second derivative is nonnegative for every a. If a=0 the function is the convex constant one, not strictly convex.

For −log x use domain (0,∞); zero and negative inputs are excluded. For x log x use the same domain and the product rule for its first derivative:

Both are strictly convex on the positive half-line. More generally xᵖ has second derivative p(p−1)xᵖ⁻², so it is convex for p≤0 or p≥1 and concave for 0≤p≤1, with affine or constant endpoint cases. This is a scalar-power result, not a matrix-power rule.

A one-variable bridge uses the mean-value theorem. If , the derivative is nondecreasing. For , the left secant slope is no larger than the right:

Rearranging gives the chord inequality. This states explicitly the mean-value theorem used to connect curvature and convexity.

Complete the least-squares task

Fit a line to readings at locations . Set and data vector :

Direct partial differentiation gives

exactly the two components of . Setting them to zero gives . Predictions are ; residuals are , squared sum , and .

The columns of are independent, so for every nonzero . Strict convexity on makes this stationary point the unique global optimizer. Nonzero residuals show that one line cannot fit all three data exactly.

Example: least squares is convex without full rank

For arbitrary m×n matrix A and b∈Rᵐ, set g(x)=‖Ax−b‖₂². Expand into quadratic, linear and constant terms before differentiating:

Every v gives vᵀ(2AᵀA)v=2‖Av‖₂²≥0, so g is convex. Full column rank makes this positive for nonzero v, giving strict convexity. Rank deficiency preserves convexity but leaves zero curvature in null directions.

An everywhere positive definite Hessian is sufficient, not necessary, for strict convexity. The strictly convex x⁴ has zero second derivative at zero. Failure of positive definiteness at one point does not disprove strict convexity.

Exercise

Find the Hessian of F(x₁,x₂)=(x₁+2x₂−1)²+4(x₁−x₂)² and test strict convexity.

Hint

Use with rows (1,2) and (2,−2).

Key steps

Write the two squares as rows of A, giving Hessian 2AᵀA. For strict convexity test whether Av=0 permits only the zero vector.

Solution and check

A is invertible, so Av=0 only for v=0. The Hessian quadratic form is positive for nonzero v and F is strictly convex.

Exercise

Find the real domains and first two derivatives of e⁻²ˣ, −log(2x+1), and (x+1)log(x+1), then test convexity.

Hint

Require positive logarithm arguments, then use the chain or product rule.

Solution and check

Each domain is an interval and each second derivative is positive there, so all three are strictly convex. For the original exponential parameter a=0 the function is constant, convex but not strictly convex.

Exercise

Is g(x)=(x₁+2x₂−1)² convex or strictly convex? How does it differ from the two-square example?

Hint

Form the rank-one Hessian and find a nonzero null direction.

Solution and check

The Hessian is PSD, so g is convex. All points with x₁+2x₂=1 attain zero, giving multiple minimizers and disproving strict convexity on R².

Start with . The inner is convex with range , the outer exponential is convex and increasing on all real inputs, and the input is convex:

The norm gives the first inner comparison, monotonicity passes it through the exponential, and outer convexity gives the last bound.

An affine inner map preserves mixtures exactly; a convex inner function gives only an inequality. If h is convex and nondecreasing, g is convex, and g(x) is in the domain of h for every x in a convex D, use monotonicity and convexity in sequence:

Since is strictly order-preserving, minimizing is equivalent to minimizing the convex score . This completes the modeling and proof chain begun in Lecture 1.

5.1 共轭：固定斜率，寻找最紧下界5.1 Conjugates: the best lower bound at a fixed slope

给定函数 f，想用直线 yx+b 从下方托住它。固定斜率 y，要求这条直线在每个允许输入 x 处都不超过 f(x)。这相当于对每个 x 都有 b≤f(x)−yx。因此能选的最大截距是这些右边的下确界。

先固定 与斜率 。配方得 ，故直线 始终位于图像下方恰好要求 。 偏低， 在 接触， 在该点超出函数。最佳截距为-2。

习惯上把这个截距的负数定义为共轭值。向量情形把乘法换成：

这里 y 固定，x 才是被优化的变量，只在 x∈dom f 上取。原函数定义域 dom f 收集允许的 x；共轭定义域 dom f 则收集使这个上确界有限的 y。有些斜率使目标无界，此时共轭值为 +∞，不存在有限截距的全局下界。若 f 从不取 −∞ 且至少一点有限，称它正常；此时 f 不会取 −∞。

正常性保证至少有一个 x₀ 使 f(x₀) 有限。对任意固定 y，共轭定义中的目标在 x₀ 处就是有限数 yᵀx₀−f(x₀)，上确界至少不小于这个数，所以不可能为 −∞。

例如 f(x)=x²/2、y=2，配方得 2x−x²/2=2−(x−2)²/2，为 2，取 x=2。因此最佳下界为 2x−2；截距 −2 是共轭值 2 的负数。

对每个固定 x，yᵀx−f(x) 关于 y 是仿射函数。第四章的上确界规则因此保证 f* 总是凸，即使原函数 f 不凸。星号的定义与第二章对偶不同；两者的联系需要具体计算，不能仅凭记号相同来判断。

这里具体引用 4.8：仿射函数都是，非空仿射函数族的逐点上确界仍凸。共轭正是这样一族以 x 为索引的仿射函数的上确界。

解答与核对

To support a function f from below with a line yx+b, fix slope y and require yx+b≤f(x) at every allowed x. Thus b≤f(x)−yx for every x, and the largest allowed intercept is the infimum of these right sides.

Fix and slope . Completing the square gives , so the line stays below the graph exactly when . Intercept minus three is low, minus two touches at two, and minus one exceeds the graph there.

Convention defines the conjugate value as the negative of that best intercept. For vectors use an :

Here y is fixed and x is optimized only over dom f. The original domain contains allowed x; the conjugate domain contains y for which that is finite. Some slopes give +∞, with no finite-intercept global lower bound. A function never −∞ and finite somewhere is called proper; its conjugate never takes −∞.

Properness supplies a point x₀ with finite f(x₀). For every fixed y, the conjugate objective at x₀ is the finite number yᵀx₀−f(x₀). Its supremum is at least that value and therefore cannot be −∞.

For f(x)=x²/2 and y=2, complete the square: 2x−x²/2=2−(x−2)²/2. The two is attained at x=2. The best lower bound is 2x−2: intercept minus two is the negative conjugate value.

For fixed x, yᵀx−f(x) is affine in y. The supremum rule makes f* convex even when f is not. This star operation differs from the dual ; their relationship requires calculation, not just matching notation.

Specifically, Section 4.8 says affine functions are convex and a pointwise supremum of a nonempty affine family remains convex. The conjugate is exactly such a supremum, indexed by x.

5.2 共轭计算：先看域，再找上界5.2 Computing conjugates: domains before derivatives

计算共轭时，固定 y 后把 yᵀx−f(x) 当作 x 的优化问题。求导只会给候选点，还要检查候选是否在域内、是否全局最大，以及边界能否使更大。下面用二次函数、指数和负对数把这套方法走完整。

正定二次函数：配方同时给界与取等

设 f(x)=xᵀPx/2，P 为实对称。以下平方项非负，故第一项是所有 x 的上界；取 x=P⁻¹y 时平方项为零，所以这个界能达到。

指数：斜率的正、零、负必须分开

取 f(x)=eˣ，域是 R。目标 q(x)=yx−eˣ。当 y>0，q′=y−eˣ=0 给 x=log y；q″=−eˣ<0，故它是唯一全局最大点，代入得 y log y−y。

y=0 时目标 −eˣ 始终小于零，x→−∞ 时才趋于零，所以上确界是零但不取得。y<0 时，x→−∞ 使 yx→+∞ 且 eˣ→0，故上确界为 +∞。这两个情形都不能通过“解导数等于零”得到。

负对数：有效斜率必须为负

f(x)=−log x，域 x>0，目标为 yx+log x。只有 y<0 时，导数 y+1/x=0 才给出域 x=−1/y。二阶导 −1/x²<0，保证它全局最大，值为 −1−log(−y)。y>0 时令 x→∞，yx 与 log x 都增大；y=0 时虽没有线性项，log x 仍趋于 +∞。因此共轭仅在 y<0 有限。

约束与线性评分：示性函数和支撑函数

非空集合 C 的示性函数 δC 在 C 内为零、外为 +∞，所以共轭只是在 C 内最大化，正是上一章的支撑函数 hC。

若 C 还是闭凸集，的共轭反过来是 δC。对 x∈C，任意 y 有 yᵀx≤hC(y)，目标不超过零，y=0 达到零。对 x∉C，分离定理给 yᵀx>hC(y)，将 y 正向放大，差值趋于 +∞。因此

注意双共轭回到各自原对象，不能把 hC 的双共轭写成 δC。一般正常函数的双共轭不超过原函数；恢复原函数需要闭凸等条件。

范数：为什么共轭只取零或无穷？

设 f(x)=N(x)。若 N(y)≤1，由对偶界，yᵀx−N(x)≤0，取 x=0 得零。若 N(y)>1，选 N(u)=1 且 yᵀu>1，再取 x=tu，t→∞，正差随 t 无界增长。因此范数的共轭是对偶的示性函数。

这里单独区分符号： 表示第二章的， 表示当前的函数共轭。前面的比较使用的正是 2.5 已证的 。

这行特意用文字区分共轭与对偶范数：左边是函数共轭运算，球约束中的 N* 才是对偶长度。阅读不同教材时，同一个星号可能承担这两种记号，必须先看定义。

补充阅读 · 其他典型函数的完整计算

仿射 f(x)=aᵀx+b 在 Rⁿ 上，目标为 (y−a)ᵀx−b。y=a 时恒为 −b；否则取 x=t(y−a)，t→∞ 便无界。因此共轭在 y=a 为 −b，其他处 +∞。

负熵项 f(x)=x log x，x>0。求导 y−log x−1=0 给 x=eʸ⁻¹，二阶导为 −1/x<0，代入得 f*(y)=eʸ⁻¹，对所有实 y 都有限且取得。

倒数 f(x)=1/x，x>0。y<0 时 y+1/x²=0，取 x=1/√(−y)，得到 −2√(−y)；目标二阶导 −2/x³<0。y=0 时 −1/x 向零逼近但不取得；y>0 时 x→∞ 无界。

范数平方 f(x)=N(x)²/2，可先固定半径 r=N(x)≥0。对偶界给 yᵀx≤rN(y)，且沿取等单位方向可达到。于是只剩最大化 rN(y)−r²/2，r=N(y) 取等，得共轭为 N(y)²/2。若原函数没有 1/2，结果是 N*(y)²/4。

矩阵例子 f(X)=−log det X，域 X≻0，内积为 tr(YX)，Y 取实对称。Y≺0 时令 Q=−Y≻0，换元 U=Q½XQ½，目标变成 log det U−tr U−log det Q。逐特征值使用 log u−u≤−1，得 −n−log det(−Y)，在 X=−Y⁻¹ 取得。

若 Y 不负定，即 Y≺0 失败，它有某个 λ≥0。在其特征坐标下令 X 对应特征值 t→∞，其他特征值固定为 1；目标含 λt+log t，必趋 +∞。因此共轭仅在 Y≺0 有限。

解答与核对

在 x=1/2，左右均为 log 2，核对接触成立。

For each fixed y, optimize yᵀx−f(x) over x. Differentiation gives candidates, not a complete answer: check membership, global optimality and boundary behavior. Quadratic, exponential and negative-logarithm examples illustrate the full method.

Positive definite quadratics: bounds and attainment

Let f(x)=xᵀPx/2 for symmetric positive definite P. The square below is nonnegative, bounding the expression for every x. Choosing x=P⁻¹y removes it and attains the bound.

Exponential: positive, zero and negative slopes

For f(x)=eˣ on R, optimize q(x)=yx−eˣ. If y>0, q′=y−eˣ=0 gives x=log y. Since q″=−eˣ<0, this is the unique global , with value y log y−y.

If y=0, −eˣ is always negative and approaches zero only as x tends to minus infinity: zero is unattained. For y<0, letting x tend to minus infinity gives yx tending to +∞ while eˣ tends to zero, so the supremum is +∞. Neither case is found by solving a stationary equation.

Negative logarithm: the slope must be negative

For f(x)=−log x on x>0, the objective is yx+log x. Only y<0 gives stationary x=−1/y. The second derivative −1/x²<0 establishes a global maximum of −1−log(−y). For y>0 both terms grow as x tends to infinity; for y=0 the logarithm alone tends to +∞. The conjugate is therefore finite only for y<0.

Constraints and scores: indicator and support

For a nonempty set C, its convex indicator δC is zero on C and +∞ elsewhere. Its conjugate simply maximizes the over C, giving the support function hC from the preceding chapter.

If C is also closed and convex, the support conjugate is δC. For x∈C, yᵀx≤hC(y) bounds the objective by zero, attained at y=0. For x outside C, separation supplies yᵀx>hC(y); scaling y makes the positive difference unbounded. Thus

Each biconjugate returns to its own original object; hC is not δC. Generally a proper function has f≤f; recovery needs closed convex assumptions.

Norms: why zero or infinity?

Let f(x)=N(x). If N(y)≤1, the dual bound gives yᵀx−N(x)≤0, attained at x=0. If N(y)>1, select N(u)=1 with yᵀu>1 and scale x=tu. The positive difference grows unboundedly. The conjugate is the indicator of the dual .

Use distinct notation here: is the dual from Chapter 2, while is the function conjugate. The comparison uses the bound proved in Section 2.5.

The annotation distinguishes conjugacy from the : the left is a function conjugate, while the ball condition uses dual length. A star can mean either operation in different texts, so check the definition.

Further reading · More standard conjugate calculations

For affine f(x)=aᵀx+b on Rⁿ, the objective is (y−a)ᵀx−b. At y=a it is constantly −b; otherwise x=t(y−a) makes it unbounded. The conjugate is −b at a and +∞ elsewhere.

For f(x)=x log x on x>0, derivative y−log x−1 gives x=eʸ⁻¹. The objective second derivative is −1/x<0 and substitution gives f*(y)=eʸ⁻¹, finite and attained for every real y.

For f(x)=1/x on x>0, y<0 gives stationary x=1/√(−y) and value −2√(−y); the objective has second derivative −2/x³<0. At y=0, −1/x approaches zero without attainment; y>0 gives unbounded growth as x tends to infinity.

For f(x)=N(x)²/2, fix r=N(x)≥0. The sharp dual bound gives yᵀx≤rN(y), attained along a maximizing unit direction. Maximize rN(y)−r²/2 over r≥0 to get N(y)²/2. Without the original factor one half, the answer is N(y)²/4.

For matrix f(X)=−log det X on X≻0, pair symmetric Y via tr(YX). If Y≺0, put Q=−Y≻0 and U=Q½XQ½. The objective becomes log det U−tr U−log det Q. Apply log u−u≤−1 to each positive to obtain −n−log det(−Y), attained at X=−Y⁻¹.

If Y≺0 fails, it has an eigenvalue λ≥0. In that eigenbasis let the corresponding eigenvalue of X be t tending to infinity and fix the others to one. The objective contains λt+log t, which is unbounded. Thus the conjugate is finite only for Y≺0.

Two computation tasks and a branch check

Treat the smooth examples and the set/norm examples as two tasks: fixed-slope branching with attainment, then encoding feasible sets as functions. For an additional branch check with , take : the conjugate values are attained at , zero unattained, and . Explain each branch before the next exercise.

正定 X 的矩阵幂由特征分解定义：Xᵖ=Qdiag(λᵢᵖ)Qᵀ。所有阶数上统一成立的结论为：−1≤p≤0 或 1≤p≤2 时矩阵凸，0≤p≤1 时矩阵凹（教材§3.6.2 Example 3.48，印刷页110 / PDF页124）。标量 xᵖ 的凸性范围更广，不能直接套来。矩阵指数 eˣ 在标量情形凸，但矩阵指数在维数≥2时一般不矩阵凸。

For vector or matrix outputs, replace scalar comparison with the order of a proper cone K from Chapter 3. The same mixture comparison defines K-convexity on a convex D.

Recall Sections 3.7 and 3.11: a is closed, convex, pointed and has nonempty interior; K*={w:wᵀd≥0 for every d∈K}. Section 3.12 characterizes a closed convex cone by all its dual scores. We use that result to turn vector inequalities into scalar inequalities.

For the nonnegative orthant, is componentwise convexity. For the PSD cone, let M be the averaged output minus the output at the mixture; matrix convexity requires M⪰0. By definition this means zᵀMz≥0 for every z, exactly the convexity inequality for the scalar function zᵀF(·)z. This proves the equivalence below; entrywise convexity is a different condition.

Example: why outer products are matrix convex

For F(x)=xxᵀ, expand the mixture gap:

The outer product is PSD since its quadratic form is a square. Thus F is matrix convex even though entry x₁x₂ is not scalar convex on R². Likewise XXᵀ is matrix convex for rectangular X because zᵀXXᵀz=‖Xᵀz‖₂² is a convex quadratic.

Check entry x₁x₂ along x=(t,−t): it becomes −t², which is not convex. Matrix convexity therefore does not require entrywise convexity.

General K-convexity is equivalent to scalar convexity of wᵀF for every w∈K*. Necessity follows from the dual definition; sufficiency follows from the closed-convex-cone dual characterization.

Further reading · Matrix powers and strict matrix convexity

For positive definite X define Xᵖ by powering its eigenvalues. Uniform operator results are matrix convexity for −1≤p≤0 or 1≤p≤2, and matrix concavity for 0≤p≤1, textbook §3.6.2, Example 3.48, printed p.110 / PDF p.124. Scalar powers have a wider convexity . The scalar exponential is convex, but the matrix exponential generally is not matrix convex in dimensions at least two.

Strict matrix convexity requires a positive definite gap for distinct inputs and nontrivial mixtures. The gap for xxᵀ has rank at most one and cannot be positive definite when the output dimension exceeds one. Do not upgrade PSD to PD.

For sufficiency, choose any ordered inputs x,y and set d=y−x∈K. Fix any w∈L* and define h(t)=wᵀF(x+td) for 0≤t≤1. Domain convexity permits the whole segment; the derivative condition yields

A nonnegative one-variable derivative makes h nondecreasing, so wᵀ(F(y)−F(x))≥0. This holds for every w∈L*, and Section 3.12 dual characterization yields F(y)−F(x)∈L, completing global monotonicity.

For linear F(x)=Ax, the condition reduces to AK⊆L. Between nonnegative orthants it means every entry of A is nonnegative, verified by testing coordinate unit vectors. For scalar output it means the lies in K*.

Before comparing inverses, justify congruence: if , then for every , giving . For invertible , applying proves the reverse implication. Both sides must use transposed factors.

Example: inversion reverses the PSD order

For A⪰B≻0, congruence by B⁻½ gives C=B⁻½AB⁻½⪰I. All eigenvalues of C are at least one, so C⁻¹⪯I. Transform back to obtain

This proves inversion is order-reversing. Next use the matrix fractional function from Section 4.5 to verify its matrix convexity. Also note that increasing scalar t² does not make matrix squaring order-preserving: with noncommuting matrices, A²−B² cannot be treated as the scalar product (A−B)(A+B).

Matrix convexity of inversion follows directly from Section 4.5: for each fixed z, zᵀX⁻¹z is a convex slice of the matrix fractional function. Apply Section 5.6 scalarization. This proof and the order-reversing argument establish separate properties.

Exercise: verify a successful order-preserving map

Does preserve orthant order? Prove it for a general difference and check .

Hint

Write and compute .

Solution and check

proves preservation. The given outputs are with nonnegative difference .

Exercise

Does A=[[1,−1],[0,2]] preserve orthant order?

Hint

Test the column containing the negative entry with a nonnegative coordinate vector.

Solution and check

No. For x=(0,0), y=(0,1), x≤y but Ax=(0,0) and Ay=(−1,2), whose first coordinate decreases. The negative entry gives a counterexample.

supremumsup

sup 是 supremum 的缩写。上确界是能够挡住所有可能数值的最小上界；它可以存在而没有任何点实际达到它。例如 x∈(0,1) 时，x 的上确界是 1，但没有最大值。The abbreviation sup stands for supremum. A supremum is the least upper bound on all possible values, and it may exist without being attained. For x∈(0,1), the supremum of x is one, but there is no maximum.

正文Read
maximummax

max 是 maximum 的缩写。说一个数是最大值，需要找到一个可行点实际取得这个数，还需要说明其他可行点都不超过它。本章的有限维闭单位球上，线性目标可以取得最大值。The abbreviation max stands for maximum. A maximum is both attained by a feasible point and at least as large as every other feasible value. The linear objective in this chapter attains a maximum on the finite-dimensional closed unit ball.

dual norm‖z‖*

先选定一个原范数，再固定向量 z。让 x 在原范数的单位球中移动，计算每个可行 x 的 zᵀx。所有这些内积的最大值，就是 z 的对偶范数。它的数值取决于原范数使用的长度规则。Choose a primal norm and fix a vector z. Let x vary over the primal unit ball and evaluate zᵀx at every feasible x. The largest value is the dual norm of z. Its value depends on the length rule used by the primal norm.

Cauchy–Schwarz inequality|uᵀv|≤‖u‖₂‖v‖₂

这个不等式给欧氏内积一个长度上界。两个非零向量同向时，uᵀv 等于长度的乘积；方向偏离时，内积会变小。本章用它先找上界，再沿正确方向构造达到上界的向量。This inequality bounds a Euclidean inner product by the product of the vector lengths. For nonzero vectors pointing in the same direction, uᵀv equals that product; changing their relative direction reduces the inner product. We use it to find a bound and then construct an attaining vector.

PD = Positive Definite，正定。这里 P 必须是实对称矩阵；对每个非零向量 x，都有 xᵀPx>0。这个条件让每一个非零方向都有正的长度代价，并保证 P 可以求逆。PD = Positive Definite（正定）. Here P is real and symmetric, and xᵀPx>0 for every nonzero vector x. Every nonzero direction therefore has a positive length cost, and P is invertible.

正文Read
